service.description: Link a git repository to a project.
Unlink a git repository from a project (the links of its commits and refs stay).

Make a git repository for a project and link it: kept on disk (local, the default for code) or in the database (db). A content repository (a web site's images, documents and media) keeps images, video, audio, PDFs and archives in Git LFS. The kind and branch not given come from the organization's repository defaults (get#RepositoryDefaults), else local and main, and those defaults' merge method and default branch rule are applied to it (apply#RepositoryDefaults).

parameter.name: repositoryId
parameter.description: The project ID in lower case when empty

parameter.name: repositoryKind
parameter.description: local or db; the organization's default, else local

return.message: A repository ID has letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-', and does not end in .git
A project repository is local or db

service.description: An organization's defaults for new project repositories (the PartySetting ProjRepositoryDefaults, a JSON object, kept small for its 255 characters, impl-projects.md F9): storage (local or db), branch (the default branch's name), mergeMethod (GmmMerge or GmmSquash), protectDefault (Y: the default branch takes no force push or delete), requireMergeRequest (Y or N), approvals (the approvals a merge needs) and dismissStale (Y: a new head sets the approvals back to requested). The organization is organizationPartyId, else the project's as ProjectServices.get#ProjectSettings finds it. Without a setting, or one that is not JSON (logged), defaults is empty and nothing is applied.

Apply an organization's repository defaults (get#RepositoryDefaults) to a new repository: its default merge method, and with protectDefault Y a branch rule on its default branch (no force push or delete, the merge request, approvals and stale approvals as the defaults say). An organization's policy applied when the repository is made, so with authorization off; a part that fails is logged and the others still apply.

parameter.name: workEffortId
parameter.description: To read the defaults when not given

service.description: The projects a git repository is linked to now.

The tasks a text names: a word that is the ID of a task of a project linked to the repository (PROJ-100023), and each Task trailer value (an ID of any task). A word right after Fix, Fixes, Fixed, Close, Closes, Closed, Resolve, Resolves or Resolved (any case) marks its task to complete. At most 50 candidate words are read.

parameter.name: trailerValues
parameter.description: The values of the Task trailers

parameter.name: projectIdList
parameter.description: The linked projects, when the caller has them

parameter.name: referenceList
parameter.description: Maps: workEffortId, rootWorkEffortId, linkSourceEnumId (WglsMessage or WglsTrailer), complete (Boolean)

service.description: Link a commit (a map as org.moqui.impl.GitServices.get#GitCommit gives it) to a work effort, unless it is linked already.

service-call.name: create#mantle.work.effort.WorkEffortGitCommit
service-call.in-map: {workEffortId:workEffortId, repositoryId:repositoryId, commitId:commit.commitId, summary:(commit.summary ?? '').substring(0, 255), authorName:commit.authorName, authorEmail:commit.authorEmail, commitDate:commit.committerDate, refName:refName, linkSourceEnumId:linkSourceEnumId, linkedByUserId:ec.user.userId, linkedDate:ec.user.nowTimestamp}

service.description: Link a commit to a task by hand, by its ID or a prefix of at least 4 hex digits.
For the commit gitECA event: link the commit to each task its message names.
Link a branch or tag to a work effort, or renew a link a deleted ref ended.

service-call.name: create#mantle.work.effort.WorkEffortGitRef

service.description: Link a branch or tag to a work effort by hand: a full ref name, or a branch or tag name.

return.message: No branch or tag ${refName} in repository ${repositoryId}

service.description: For the tag event and a branch's ref-update create event: link the ref to the work efforts its name names, under the projects linked to the repository. A tag: the name before its first '/' is the ID of the project, a milestone or a task (PROJ/v1.0, PROJ-100023/review, or PROJ-100023 alone); an annotated tag's message names tasks as a commit message does; a tag named as a release's version, or v and the version (1.4.0, v1.4.0), links that release of a linked project. A branch: its last path segment, or the part of it before a '-', is the ID of a task (PROJ-100023, feature/PROJ-100023-login-fix).

set.from: candidateIds.map(id => namedList.find(we => we.workEffortId == id)).find(we => we != null && (isTag ? (projectIdList.includes(we.workEffortId) || projectIdList.includes(we.rootWorkEffortId)) : (we.workEffortTypeEnumId == 'WetTask' && projectIdList.includes(we.rootWorkEffortId))))

service.description: For a ref-update delete event: end the links of a deleted branch or tag.

For a ref-update event of the default branch: complete (and resolve) each task a commit the branch gained names after Fixes, Closes or Resolves. Only commits made after the repository was linked to the task's project count, so the first fetch of a mirror does not complete tasks from old history; a task already complete, closed or cancelled, or whose status flow has no way to Complete from where it is, is left.
Complete and resolve a task when its status flow allows it from where it is.

log.message: Task ${workEffortId} named by commit ${commitId} cannot go from ${task.statusId} to WeComplete

service.description: Link a merge request to the work items it names, in the projects its repository is linked to: the task its source branch is named for (as link#RefByName reads a branch: its last path segment, or the part of it before a '-'), and the keys in its title and description (find#TaskReferences). completeOnMerge: a Closes, Fixes or Resolves keyword before the key, completeItems when given, else the project's WstMergeRequestMoves. A text link whose key is gone from the text is removed; branch and hand-made links stay. The rule of the merge request's opened and updated events (handle#MergeRequestEvent), so with authorization off.

parameter.name: completeItems
parameter.description: Every linked item completes on merge (true) or only the Closes ones (false); the project's WstMergeRequestMoves when empty

service.description: Link a work item to a merge request by hand (MergeRequestDetail's Link), for a user who may view the merge request's repository; completeOnMerge Y completes the item when it merges.
Unlink a work item from a merge request, for a user who may view the merge request's repository.
The work items linked to a merge request, for a user who may view its repository: workEffortId, workEffortName, statusId, status, rootWorkEffortId, linkSourceEnumId, linkSource, completeOnMerge.

On a merged merge request, complete (and resolve) its work items linked with completeOnMerge Y, each where its status flow allows (complete#TaskFromCommit, with the merge commit); an item that does not complete is logged and the others still do.

A merge request opened or marked ready: its linked work items in progress (or approved) move to In Review where their status flow has it (set#TaskStatus), when their project's WstMergeRequestMoves is Y. An item that does not move is logged and the others still do.

The gitECA-style rules of a merge request's events (service/Work.secas.xml, after the framework's org.moqui.impl.GitReviewServices services): opened, updated, ready and reopened link its work items (link#MergeRequestItems), and opened or ready move them to In Review (move#MergeRequestItemsToReview); merged completes them (complete#MergeRequestItems); and the reviewers and the author are told (topics MergeRequestReview and MergeRequestUpdate, notify#MergeRequest). synchronize (a new head of the source) marks the review threads it changed outdated (refresh#ReviewAnchors). Each rule on its own: one that fails is logged, the others and the change itself stand.

parameter.name: action
parameter.description: opened, updated, ready, reviewed, synchronize, closed, reopened, merged or review_requested

parameter.name: actorUserId
parameter.description: Who made the change; the current user when empty

service.description: Tell users of a merge request's change: kind review (topic MergeRequestReview) the reviewers asked (userIdList, else every reviewer still requested); kind update (topic MergeRequestUpdate, with change: approved, requested changes, reviewed, commented, pushed new commits, merged, closed) its author and reviewers. Never the one who made the change. Message: mergeRequestId, mergeRequestNum, title, repositoryId, sourceRef, targetRef, actorName, change, the merge request as the record. A notice that fails is logged.

A failure or error status posted on a commit (the SECA on org.moqui.impl.GitServices.create#GitCommitStatus): topic CommitStatusFailed to the commit's author (its Moqui-User-Id, else the user accounts with its email) and to the authors of the open merge requests whose head it is, not the one who posted it. Message: repositoryId, commitId, shortId, summary, checkContext (a template's context names the context itself), state, stateLabel, description, targetUrl. A notice that fails is logged.

A comment on a merge request by the current user, who may view its repository: a CommunicationEvent of type Comment (markdown) filed on the merge request (CommunicationEventRecord), on a line of its diff when path and a line are given (store#ReviewAnchor), or a reply to a thread (parentCommEventId). The author and reviewers are told (MergeRequestUpdate, commented).

Put a merge request's comment on a line of its diff (CommunicationEventGitAnchor), at the source's current head unless commitId is given; for a user who may view the repository. The comment must be filed on the merge request.

Resolve a review thread, or reopen it (resolved false): its first comment, the one with the anchor, goes to CeResolved and back to CeSent (a direct change: the Default flow of communication events has neither move from a sent comment). For a user who may view the merge request's repository; given a reply, its thread.

The line comments of a merge request, for a user who may view its repository: each thread (its first comment with the anchor) with path, oldLine, newLine, lineText, commitId, outdated, resolved, and its comments in order (communicationEventId, fromPartyId, authorName, entryDate, body). With path, the threads of that file.

A merge request's source has a new head: each thread on a new line read at an older head is outdated when the line changed since (a deleted or changed line in the diff from its head to the new one, or its file gone). One that cannot be checked is logged and left as it is.

The branch name for a work item by its project's pattern (WstBranchPattern, else <id>-<words>): <id> the item's ID (PROJ-12), <KEY> and <key> the project's ID as it is and in lower case, <n> the number after the item ID's last '-', <words> up to six words of its name in lower case joined by '-', <type> fix, feature, docs or task by its purpose. Letters, digits, '.', '_', '-' and '/' are kept.

A branch for a work item (WorkItemDetail's Create branch): named by get#TaskBranchName unless branchName is given, in repositoryId or the one repository of its project, from a ref (the default branch's head when empty), made by org.moqui.impl.GitServices.create#GitRef (the user's create right and the branch rules apply) and linked to the item (store#WorkEffortRef).

The palette's Code group (design-projects.md §1.4): repositories by id or description, and merge requests by number (!12, or #12) or title, of the repositories the user may view; archived repositories are left out. resultList: kind (repository or mergeRequest), repositoryId, description, and for a merge request mergeRequestId, mergeRequestNum, title, statusId, sourceRef, targetRef. The app makes them links.

The authzServiceName of the ALL_USERS grant on the GitRepositories artifact group (design-projects.md §7, §15 "Repository access by role"), by the user's party's current WorkEffortParty roles on the projects the repository is linked to: an internal member may view it and push new refs and fast-forwards (AUTHZA_VIEW, AUTHZA_CREATE, AUTHZA_UPDATE); a lead of such a project (ProjectManager, Manager, ProgrammerLead, SysArchitect) also force-pushes and deletes refs and changes the settings (AUTHZA_DELETE); a client contact (Customer, CustomerBillTo, ClientManager, ClientBilling) only views it, and only when that project shares its repositories with the client (WorkEffortSetting WstShareRepositories Y). A client contact who signs in (the PROJECT_CLIENT permission, ProjectServices.get#ClientProjectInfo: its party's or its organization's client role on a project that allows client sign-in) only views the repositories of its client projects that share them, whatever other role its party holds (impl-projects.md P10). For anyone else nothing (AUTHZT_NONE), so other grants decide.
